rv.q: This play is a must see, maybe twice, you're bound to miss something.
Marie Antoinette and the Magical Negroes is one of those plays that I am positive will stick with me for a long time.
Still, its disjointed narrative will cause season theater audiences to leave wondering what message it was trying to provide.
Guest in this piece has risen up as one of Chicago's freshest and most daring storytellers.
Alan Bresloff 4 years ago [rating=2]Great acting and impressive choreography cannot save the play “Marie Antoinette and the Magical Negroes”, written and directed by Terry Guest.

cn.t: Critics are sharply divided on this provocative exploration of Black revolution through a French Revolution lens. Strong performances and bold vision earn praise, but the violent imagery and heavy-handed approach alienate some.
